job.style: a comparison of two related ideas

passage: Plastic is a synthetic material derived primarily from petrochemicals, not natural sources like wood or plants. Unlike organic matter, plastic does not biodegrade; it merely breaks down into smaller fragments known as microplastics. These microplastics are not living organisms, but tiny, persistent synthetic particles that accumulate in the food chain, posing severe risks to wildlife. Many people mistakenly believe that burning plastic is a safe disposal method, but this process releases toxic chemicals into the air, which are far more hazardous than the smoke produced by burning wood. Furthermore, burying plastic in a landfill does not solve the problem, as the material remains intact for centuries, potentially leaching chemicals into the soil and groundwater. Even items labeled as 'biodegradable' often require specific industrial conditions to break down and will not rot away in a standard dustbin or the ocean. Finally, recycling is not a perfect solution because plastic quality degrades with each cycle, and mixed, dirty plastics are often impossible to process, meaning they eventually end up as waste regardless of the recycling symbol on the packaging.

items.evidence: Even items labeled as 'biodegradable' often require specific industrial conditions to break down and will not rot away in a standard dustbin or the ocean.
items.q: Meera throws a plastic bag labelled 'biodegradable' into the sea. What will most likely happen to it?
options: It will last, since it needs factory conditions to break
It will rot quickly, since the label promises it will
It will vanish, since it breaks into tiny pieces
It will rot in a few years, just like paper
items.explain: Biodegradable plastics often need special industrial conditions to break down, so they will not rot away in the ocean.

wrong.why: thinks anything labelled biodegradable rots quickly anywhere
thinks tiny pieces have disappeared from the environment
thinks plastic disappears in a few years like paper

items.evidence: Many people mistakenly believe that burning plastic is a safe disposal method, but this process releases toxic chemicals into the air, which are far more hazardous than the smoke produced by burning wood.
items.q: Aman wants to get rid of plastic waste by burning it like dry leaves. Why is this a bad idea?
options: It gives off poisonous gases worse than wood smoke
It wastes plastic that could be recycled forever
It harms only fish once the ash reaches the sea
It spreads microplastic germs that grow in the air
items.explain: Burning plastic releases toxic chemicals into the air, far more harmful than smoke from burning wood.

wrong.why: thinks plastic can be recycled forever without losing quality
thinks only sea animals are harmed by plastic

items.evidence: Furthermore, burying plastic in a landfill does not solve the problem, as the material remains intact for centuries, potentially leaching chemicals into the soil and groundwater.
items.q: A town buries all its plastic waste in a landfill. What will the plastic be like after fifty years?
options: It stays whole and may pollute soil and water
It rots away fully, just like paper does
It breaks into tiny bits and is gone for good
It turns back into wood and plant matter
items.explain: Buried plastic remains intact for centuries and can leach chemicals into the soil and groundwater.

wrong.why: thinks plastic disappears in a few years like paper
thinks tiny pieces have disappeared from the environment
thinks plastic is made from natural things like wood and plants

items.evidence: Finally, recycling is not a perfect solution because plastic quality degrades with each cycle, and mixed, dirty plastics are often impossible to process, meaning they eventually end up as waste regardless of the recycling symbol on the packaging.
items.q: Sunil puts dirty, mixed plastic packets marked with the triangle symbol into a bin. What will most likely happen to them?
options: They will probably end up as waste anyway
They will be recycled, since the symbol says so
They will be recycled forever, staying good as new
They will be cleaned and sorted, then recycled easily
items.explain: Mixed, dirty plastics are often impossible to process, so they end up as waste whatever the recycling symbol says.

wrong.why: thinks the recycling symbol means it will be recycled
thinks plastic can be recycled again and again with no loss
thinks dirty mixed plastic can be recycled together
